title: Multiplexed Single-molecule Force Proteolysis Measurements Using Magnetic Tweezers
protocol: Clean coverslips using sonication.
Add coverslips to a small glass container.
Fill the container with isopropanol.
Sonicate in a bath sonicator for 20 minutes.
Discard isopropanol and rinse coverslips with deionized water.
Fill container with water and sonicate for 20 minutes.
Dry coverslips using filtered, dust-free air.
Flame the coverslips gently to remove any remaining dust and moisture.
Attach two coverslips together using double-sided scotch tape.
Cut tape to a length of ~3 cm and width of 0.3 cm.
Attach tape on 22x40 mm coverslip leaving a 1.6 cm channel in the middle.
Use pipette tip to press down gently on the coverslip to ensure proper adhesion.
Mix 50 μL of 4 nM λ-DNA with 2 μL of 40 nM biotin conjugated oligonucleotide.
Heat the mixture at 60 °C for 10 minutes.
Slowly cool the mixture to room temperature over 1 hour.
Add DNA ligase according to manufacturer's specifications and ligate at room temperature for 3 hours.
Add 2 μL of 400 nM digoxigenin conjugated oligonucleotide and incubate at room temperature for 45 minutes.
Add 1.5 μL of 10 mM ATP and continue ligation of the digoxigenin conjugated oligonucleotide to the λ-DNA for 3 hours.
Remove excess oligonucleotides and DNA ligase using 100 kDa spin filters (Microcon Ultracell YM-100).
Exchange buffer a total of 1000-fold in TE buffer.
Examine a sample of the DNA via electrophoresis on a 0.7% agarose gel to ensure that the DNA is not denatured or sheared.
Measure DNA concentration using a Nanodrop UV-Vis spectrometer.
Prepare flow cells as described in section 1.
Add anti-digoxigenin antibody (1 μg mL-1) to the flow cell and allow it to adhere for 15 minutes.
Passivate the surface of the flow cell by adding 2 mg mL-1 BSA, 0.1% Tween-20 in 1x PBS and incubate at room temperature for 45 minutes.
Add 50 pM functionalized λ-DNA and allow it to attach to the coverslip for 15 minutes.
Wash away excess DNA with 1x PBS.
Add streptavidin-coated superparamagnetic beads (2 μg mL-1 or 20 μg mL-1) and allow them to attach to the immobilized DNA for 15 minutes.
Wash away excess beads with 1x PBS.
Move permanent magnets far from the sample surface (>15 mm).
Place prepared flow cell in the microscope.
Move permanent magnets into position above the flow cell.
Choose focal plane of λ-DNA functionalized beads by focusing on bright center of beads.
Take a video of bead motion at 80 Hz or greater for 500 frames.
Move the magnet closer to the sample surface in 1 mm increments for distances beyond 5 mm.
Move the magnet closer to the sample surface in 0.5 mm increments for distances between 1 and 5 mm.
Move the magnet closer to the sample surface in 0.25 mm increments for distances less than 1 mm.
Repeat steps 2.11.5 and 2.11.6 at each new magnet position.
Track the center of the beads using a 2D Gaussian fit for each data set.
Calculate the force via Brownian fluctuations using the provided formula.
Confirm the accuracy of the forces by checking the force calculation via a power spectrum Lorentzian fit to find the rolloff frequency.
Relate applied force to the rolloff frequency using the provided relation.
Add anti-myc (15 μg mL-1) to the flow cell and incubate at room temperature for 20 minutes.
Passivate the flow cell using 5 mg mL-1 BSA in PBS buffer.
Add 150 pM collagen peptide and allow it to attach to the antibody via the myc tag for 45 minutes.
Wash away excess collagen using PBS buffer.
Mix streptavidin-coated superparamagnetic 1 μm beads with collagen molecules in PBS.
Incubate for 45 minutes to allow bead attachment to collagen molecules.
Separate 3 μm beads from the solution using strong magnets.
Resolubilize separated 3 μm beads in PBS.
Repeat separation and resolubilization of 3 μm beads three times.
Image the flow cell containing collagen peptide and magnetic beads under low force (~1 pN) in the magnetic trap.
Apply modest force to liberate weakly adhered beads from the surface.
Add pre-activated MMP-1 enzyme, which was activated by adding 3.5 mM APMA and incubated at 37°C for 3 hours, to the flow cell.
Record a video of several fields of view immediately after introducing the flow cell into the magnetic tweezers apparatus (t = 0).
Repeat recording of several fields of view at regular time points until all beads detach or no further proteolysis is discernable.
Count the beads in the various fields of view at different time points.
Average the counted bead numbers for each time point.
Normalize the average number of beads at each time point by dividing by the number of beads at t = 0.
Plot the ratio as a function of time.
Fit the plot to an exponential decay plus a constant.
Repeat the experiment under varying force conditions and MMP-1 concentrations.
